beats.headline: The mount he left behind
beats.text: Sierra, Northropi Vampire, level sixty-five neighbourhood boss, is a Bereft Minion of Viscount Fog. The description is the file on both of them. The great, now-deceased hunter of vampires trained Sierra never to leave his side, and together they hunted the scourge that took his village and family. When he learned of a new bloodsucker named Miriam Dom, he set out to exterminate her. It went bad. Sierra was injured by the bloodsucker trying to save him, fled, and is now what they both hated.

beats.headline: The star of Blood Hunter
beats.text: Crawler Miriam Dom, in a forest clearing, fills in the rest. Viscount Fog was an elite hunting her from the moment she landed, the star of one of the programmes run inside the dungeon, called Blood Hunter. His first attack came while she and Prepotente were fighting Big Tina. The climax was written in advance: the vampirism curse would spread through the forest, Fog would kill its progenitor, which is Miriam, and every infected dinosaur would be cured, stopping an apocalypse.

beats.headline: Community Pool, returned to sender
beats.text: The second attack. Prepotente reads Community Pool, which moves an infection from one party to another and would have made Fog the head vampire. Viscount Fog counters, throwing the spell back. Prepotente's Opposite Day ring throws it at Fog again, and Fog has a ring of his own. The spell ping-pongs between them several times in under a second. Both are stunned repeatedly, and the stuns compound. Past the third, the sufferer becomes Fragile, and the slightest damage kills.

beats.headline: Dust, at sunset
beats.text: The bounced spell came out inside out, as spells that bounce often enough do. Viscount Fog took a new debuff, Cursed Light Walker: where a vampire dies in light, his health seeped away out of it. Crawler Miriam Dom had him stunned and helpless and did not strike, in case he had one trick left that would take Prepotente with him. She did not need to. Frozen and unable to heal, he died when the sun set and crumpled to dust.
